subject: general
question: Who among the following had written the novel ‘Untouchable’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mulk Raj Anand**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mulk Raj Anand's 'Untouchable' is a novel about a day in the life of one of **India's lowest untouchables, sweepers who clean up the excreta left by the poor who do not have access to toilets or even outhouses.**
 
• It narrates the sufferings and humiliations of an **18-year-old boy, Bakha, born in a low-caste and serving as a toilet sweeper.**
 
• At that time, the caste system had been in place for over two thousand years. Society was divided into four tiers of privilege. The highest ranks comprise the wealthy, the intellectuals, and other positions of power.
 
• The Untouchables were actually even lower than the lowest caste, comprising a fifth class outside of rank, and are seen as filthy, even to the point of being able to pollute upper caste members through their touch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mulk Raj Anand (1905 – 2004) along with** R. K. Narayan (1906 – 2001), Ahmad Ali (1910 -1994), and Raja Rao (1908 – 2006)** is considered some of the pioneers of Indo-Anglian fiction.

 
 
• He was known for his depiction of the lives of the poorer castes in traditional Indian society and was one of the first India-based writers in English to gain an international readership. 
 
• He was a recipient of the Padma Bhushan.
